one_line: This video demonstrates how photographic variables like lighting, distance, tilt, and expression can mimic or exaggerate plastic surgery results.

hook.what_happens: A side-by-side comparison of a woman's face labeled 'Before' and 'After' asks 'What else changed?'
hook.why_it_works: It challenges the viewer's perception of standard cosmetic surgery results.

onscreen_text.text: One of these is before surgery. One is after. Watch what else changed.
In most before-and-afters, the surgery isn't the only thing that moved. Four other things
One. The light. Flat light from the front erases most of the shadow on a face. Move it overhead and the folds and hollows come straight back. Same face, nothing touched.
Two. The distance. A phone at arm's length pushes the nose forward and pulls the jaw in. Two steps back, and the whole face rebalances, with nothing done to it.
Three. The tilt. Chin down hides a jawline. Chin level gives you one. That's a few degrees.
Four. The face you're making. A relaxed mouth and a slight lift move the midface before anyone has touched it.
None of this means the surgery did nothing. It means you can't separate the surgery from the photograph by looking at it. Both are true at
So test it yourself. Two photos, same room, a minute apart. Light in front, then light above. You'll meet two different people.
1 Two photos, same room, a minute apart.
2 One with the light in front of you.
3 One with the light above you.
The only comparison worth anything is the same face, same light, same lens, same angle. Ask any gallery for that. Or see it on your own face first.

narrative_arc: Introduce the illusion of before/after plastic surgery photos.
Identify the four key photographic variables.
Demonstrate the impact of lighting changes.
Demonstrate the impact of camera distance.
Demonstrate the impact of head tilt.
Demonstrate the impact of facial expression.
Conclude that photos cannot be separated from the surgery itself.
Provide a call to action to try the experiment or search for Refina AI.

Relatable DIY experiment encourages viewer engagement.

animations.name: Before/After Slider Reveal
animations.what_moves: A vertical divider sweeps across the face, revealing the 'After' jawline on the right and 'Before' on the left.
animations.purpose: To demonstrate the subtle difference in jawline definition before and after a procedure.
animations.reusable_as: Comparing any two states of a product, cosmetic result, or photo edit.

animations.name: Drawn Callouts
animations.what_moves: Four numbered labels with leader lines pointing to specific facial features.
animations.purpose: To break down the four photographic variables that change between before-and-after photos.
animations.reusable_as: Highlighting key features or ingredients of a product in a diagrammatic way.

animations.name: Interactive Light Source
animations.what_moves: A yellow dot representing the key light moves from the side to overhead, while the facial shadows morph dynamically.
animations.purpose: To visually demonstrate how changing the light angle dramatically alters the appearance of facial shadows and wrinkles.
animations.reusable_as: Showing 3D lighting effects on products, packaging, or architectural renders.
animations.would_need_building: A synchronized light-source controller that maps a draggable or animated handle to a sequence of frames with varying light angles.

animations.name: Distance Perspective Slider
animations.what_moves: A slider handle moves along a scale, and the face image transitions between wide-angle (close) and telephoto (far) perspectives.
animations.purpose: To show how camera distance distorts facial features (nose size vs. jaw width).
animations.reusable_as: Demonstrating focal length differences, zoom capabilities, or spatial depth in product photography.
animations.would_need_building: A perspective slider component that morphs or crossfades between different focal lengths based on slider position.

animations.name: Highlight Circle
animations.what_moves: A hand-drawn style white circle outlines the nasolabial fold.
animations.purpose: To draw immediate focus to the specific facial fold being discussed in the voiceover.
animations.reusable_as: Highlighting a specific detail, flaw, or feature in a product demonstration.

animations.name: Facial Mesh Overlay
animations.what_moves: A 3D-like wireframe grid draws itself over the subject's forehead and face.
animations.purpose: To represent scientific analysis, facial mapping, or AI tracking of facial features.
animations.reusable_as: Tech-focused ads, facial recognition concepts, or mapping product contours.
animations.would_need_building: A complex multi-path SVG wireframe that animates its stroke-dashoffset to simulate a 3D scan.

animations.name: Step List
animations.what_moves: Numbered list items fade in sequentially.
animations.purpose: To present a clear, step-by-step instruction for the viewer to try at home.
animations.reusable_as: How-to guides, recipe steps, or feature lists.

animations.name: Button Grid Pop-In
animations.what_moves: Four rounded buttons pop into a 2x2 grid.
animations.purpose: To present the key criteria for a fair comparison in a clean, interactive-looking layout.
animations.reusable_as: Displaying categories, tags, or feature highlights at the end of an ad.

signature_moves: Interactive slider reveals showing before/after states
Dynamic lighting and perspective morphs controlled by UI elements
Clean, technical vector overlays (callouts, meshes) drawing on top of photography
animation_language_summary.how_things_enter: Elements generally scale up with a slight elastic bounce (PopIn) or draw on using stroke animations (TrimPath).
animation_language_summary.how_things_leave: Elements typically fade out or are wiped away by the next transition.
animation_language_summary.how_scenes_change: Hard cuts are used to transition between different analytical concepts, keeping the focus on the central face portrait.
animation_language_summary.what_stays_still: The subject's face remains centered and aligned across almost all scenes to maintain a direct comparison.
animation_language_summary.rhythm: Bursty and educational. Periods of static observation are punctuated by smooth, interactive-feeling demonstrations (sliding, lighting shifts) to prove the scientific points.

what_we_should_steal: The Interactive Light Source morphing effect to show dynamic lighting changes on a static subject.
The Distance Perspective Slider to demonstrate focal length and camera distance distortion.
The clean, technical 3D Facial Mesh Overlay for tech-focused or scientific branding.
